metadata.title: The bridged cross-polytope framework: unit-spring elastic constants in every dimension and an exact motion from the CaB6 boron net to face-centred cubic packing
metadata.description:
Version 2, superseding v1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23322080), whose novelty claims for the rigidity counts are corrected. For the periodic framework of regular cross-polytopes joined by bars (the same periodic graph as Borcea and Streinu 2021, Section 7), we prove that with unit springs every shear modulus vanishes, C11/C12 = (n-1)^2 and the Poisson ratio is 1/(n^2-n-1), for every dimension n >= 3; the zero-mode and self-stress counts are lemmas following from existing periodic-rigidity machinery. In three dimensions we give an exact continuous motion, rational in one parameter over Q(sqrt2), that keeps every bar length, holds the octahedra in fixed orientation while the lattice deforms, raises the packing density strictly from 0.2233 to pi/sqrt18 and ends at face-centred cubic packing, with non-overlap proven. Secondary results: a radius-ratio identity and the exact CaB6-type packing maximum. The archive contains the preprint, the interactive site, replayable verifiers and certificates. Not peer reviewed.

Corrections (2026-11-03)

  • Elastic qualifiers: the unit-spring result holds for every dimension n >= 3. "All shear moduli zero" should read C44 = 0, meaning every stiffness component involving a cube-axis shear strain vanishes; it does not claim that every rotated shear has zero stiffness. C11/C12 = (n-1)^2, and the Poisson ratio 1/(n^2-n-1) is for uniaxial stress along a cube axis (nu_100).
  • Borcea and Streinu (2021), Section 7, describe the same infinite framework at a different bar length and with a different periodicity lattice. The counts here are per cell of 2Z^n. A failed literature search does not establish novelty.
  • AI assistance: computation, proofs, checking and writing across the project used AI models under the author's direction: Claude models from Anthropic (including Claude Opus 5.5), GPT-6 via Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI), and Muse, an AI agent by Meta, used at times to review and proofread the work. The GitHub user abu-aska proofread the research; proofreading is not a check of the proofs. The recorded reviews of the proofs were done by AI models; the repository does not document a human proof-checking scope, and independent human mathematical review is pending. Roles are recorded in CONTRIBUTORS.md.
  • Licences: text, figures and site content are CC BY 4.0; code is MIT. Third-party material keeps its own terms (NOTICE). 25 CIF files in research/chemistry/cod were provided by IUCr Journals for scientific use with attribution to the source article; neither licence above covers them. Whether future archives keep these files is an open decision.

The archived files and their hashes are unchanged.

Corrected version: v3.0.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23841188.
